subject.title: Feature: groupScope option to consolidate group sessions into main

question: Should OpenClaw support routing a group chat into an agent’s main session, and if so should that capability be limited to explicit per-binding opt-in or also include a global groupScope default?
rationale: This is a deliberate context-sharing boundary: a correct implementation can still expose private main-session context to group participants, and code review cannot choose the acceptable product policy alone.

options.title: Per-binding opt-in only
options.body: Allow a named binding to select the main session while retaining isolated groups as the only global behavior, with prominent documentation of the context-sharing boundary.

options.title: Global and binding scopes
options.body: Accept the linked PR’s symmetric global groupScope plus per-binding override shape, provided precedence, defaults, and group-to-main exposure are documented and tested.

options.title: Keep group sessions isolated
options.body: Reject main-session folding for groups and direct users toward separate shared-session designs that do not merge private DM context.

recommendation.title: Per-binding opt-in only
recommendation.body: Allow a named binding to select the main session while retaining isolated groups as the only global behavior, with prominent documentation of the context-sharing boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history ties this person most directly to the session-routing and group/channel behavior that defines the boundary.
